description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) percentage of different methods as a function of the co-occurrence number. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," is on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^3. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", ranges from 60% to 80%. The plot includes six lines, each representing a different method: Base (black line with circle markers), MEND (brown line with diamond markers), FT (blue line with triangle markers), MEMIT (purple line with pentagon markers), IKE (red line with triangle markers), and ROME (green line with square markers). The Base method starts at approximately 62% accuracy at the lowest co-occurrence number and ends around 66% at the highest co-occurrence number. MEND begins at about 64% and ends near 68%. FT starts at around 63% and finishes close to 67%. MEMIT begins at approximately 65% and ends at about 67%. IKE starts at around 64% and ends near 66%. ROME begins at about 66% and ends at approximately 68%. All lines show a general upward trend, indicating an increase in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases.
